title: What Happens When Half Your Raw Study Vanishes Within One Hour?
description:
Clinical Case Briefing — Hermann Ebbinghaus (1885): 2,300 Nonsense Syllables ('WID, ZOF, KAF') & the Brutal Mathematics of Forgetting, grounded in Hermann Ebbinghaus (1913) ([English scholarly edition of Hermann Ebbinghaus's 1885 Über das Gedächtnis self-experimentation monograph]). Empirical findings show that in the late 1870s, Wilhelm Wundt declared 'higher mental processes like memory can NEVER be measured experimentally.' Hermann Ebbinghaus disagreed — and spent 1879-1880 and 1883-1884 alone in Berlin testing his own memory with ruthless mathematical discipline (Über das Gedächtnis, 1885).

Follow-up physiological and behavioral evidence demonstrates: To strip away prior poetry or word meanings, Ebbinghaus constructed ~2,300 consonant-vowel-consonant 'nonsense syllables' (like WID, ZOF, KAF, DAX), drew random lists of 13 syllables, and read them aloud at a strict 150-strokes-per-minute metronome beat (0.4 s per syllable) at the exact same hour each day.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Hermann Ebbinghaus (1913). Memory: A contribution to experimental psychology. [English scholarly edition of Hermann Ebbinghaus's 1885 Über das Gedächtnis self-experimentation monograph]. https://doi.org/10.1037/10011-000
- Horst U. K. Gundlach (1986). Ebbinghaus, nonsense syllables, and three-letter words. Contemporary Psychology: A Journal of Reviews. https://doi.org/10.1037/024860
- Fred Strassburger (1959). THE DISCREPANCY HYPOTHESIS OF AFFECT AND ASSOCIATION VALUE OF NONSENSE SYLLABLES. Psychological Reports. https://doi.org/10.2466/pr0.5.528-528

AI Disclosure: Visual reenactments, 3D anatomical models, and narration in this documentary Short were produced with AI synthesis tools from verified peer-reviewed sources.
